title: Nonemptiness of the finite upper image
statement: Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff function, and let $u$ be a finite sample of columns from $Y$. If $X$ is nonempty, then the finite upper image $U(X,f,u)$ is nonempty; that is, there exists a vector $z : u \to \bbr$ for which some $x \in X$ satisfies $f(x,y) < z_y$ for every $y \in u$.
hypotheses_covered: $u$ is a finite sample of columns from $Y$
$f$ is a real payoff function on $\bbr \times \bbr$
replaced:
If $X$ is nonempty, then for every finite column sample $u$ the upper image
$U(X,f,u)$ is nonempty.
